title: Concurrent first-user registration can create multiple admin accounts

evidence.quote: Register the first admin user. This endpoint only works when no users exist.
is_admin=True,  # First user is always admin

reasoning: The route enforces the single first-admin rule with a read-before-write check, then creates and commits the admin user later. If two registration requests reach different workers or processes while the database is empty, both can observe no existing user and both can commit distinct admin accounts. A username uniqueness constraint does not prevent this when the requests use different usernames.
reproduction: Against an empty database, send two concurrent POST requests to /auth/register with different usernames. Both can pass the empty-user check before either commit is visible, resulting in two users with is_admin=True.
recommendation: Make the setup check and user creation atomic. For SQLite, acquire a write transaction before checking for existing users and recheck inside that transaction, or introduce a database-backed singleton/setup lock and translate integrity failures into 403/409 responses.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and the inspected test search did not find registration-route tests or a concurrent first-registration case.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a pytest that runs two concurrent registration requests against an empty test database with distinct usernames, then asserts exactly one request succeeds and the users table contains exactly one admin user.
minimumFixScope: Update app/api/auth.py to perform the no-users check and insert under an atomic database transaction; add a migration/model change only if the chosen fix uses a DB-level singleton constraint.
